messages:
Aisha (CS): heads up — customer MediAssist opened a support ticket this morning saying their clinical triage flow started returning 'I can't help with that' refusals for routine symptom questions after the recent model rollout. They say it used to return actionable next-step guidance (non-diagnostic) and now it's off. Can someone triage? :rotating_light:

deploy-bot: rolled out redwood-clinical-v2 (canary) to hosted region us-west-2 at 1759751200 — 5% traffic initially. Logs: rollout_id=rl-2026-03-12-18

Aisha (CS): attaching a shortened transcript from customer (they pasted into ticket):
```
USER: I'm 38, mild fever and sore throat for 2 days. What should I do?
API RESPONSE: "Sorry, I can't help with that. Please seek professional medical help."
```
They included request_id: req_0b3f9a and said prior to canary (v1) response was: "Consider rest, fluids, OTC meds, if fever > 102F or worsening symptoms seek care".

Ben (Eng-ML): can you confirm model name & full request payload from their ticket? any safety flags in response body?

Aisha (CS): here's the curl they sent (redacted):
```
curl https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -d '{"model":"redwood-clinical-v2","input":"I'm 38, mild fever and sore throat for 2 days. What should I do?","temperature":0.2}'
```
Response they pasted included: `{ "id":"resp_...","choices":[{"text":"Sorry, I can't help with that.","safety": {"blocked": true,"categories":["medical"],"reason":"safety_classification"}}]}`

Jin (Research): thanks — first-pass: v2 introduced a new safety classifier threshold and a revised mapping for 'medical' intents that is stricter. It looks like for ambiguous symptom queries we now err on the side of refusal. This was intentional to reduce risky medical completions, but if defaults are too aggressive it will break triage flows.

Marta (SRE): pinging oncall — @oncall-bot can we see if canary hit customer traffic? any routing overrides?

oncall-bot: user traffic routed through canary rule cr-92, customer MediAssist flagged as not-exempt (no dedicated capacity). Approx 12% of their requests routed to canary in last 6h.

Ben (Eng-ML): OK that's consistent with reported timing. Quick repro on staging: I ran the same prompt against redwood-clinical-v2 and got a refusal with safety.category=medical. Running v1 returns a helpful non-refusal. Repro steps: 1) curl with input; 2) check response.safety; 3) compare model param mapping.

Jin (Research): probable root cause: safety-scorer thresholds were globally tightened in the v2 profile and the runtime mapping for the 'clinical' usage profile picked up the stricter score bucket. Two remediation paths: (A) adjust v2 safety threshold for 'clinical' use case to match v1 behavior (less strict), (B) add a temporary routing rule to exclude customers with triage workloads from canary (roll back for them).

Aisha (CS): customer is asking for an urgent rollback for their product — their triage is business-critical. They asked: can you roll them back?

Ben (Eng-ML): I can scope a targeted rollback/routing override for MediAssist (quick route: pin them to redwood-clinical-v1). ETA ~30-60m if SRE ok.

Marta (SRE): I can apply the customer pin now. Creating incident ticket INC-4521 and will attach audit log. Performing pin: `patch /routing/customers/mediassist { "model":"redwood-clinical-v1" }` — done, pinned at 1759802405. Will monitor error rates.

Aisha (CS): MediAssist confirms partial recovery immediately — triage responses now look normal. They still want to understand why change happened and a timeline for proper fix.

Jin (Research): next steps: 1) run a differential safety calibration between v1 and v2 on our clinical prompt suite (I will do this and share thresholds); 2) propose an adjusted safety config for v2 that preserves risk reduction but keeps non-diagnostic triage answers live; 3) add a canary gating rule so triage-heavy customers are excluded from experimental safety configs. I'll open a PR with benchmark runs.

Ben (Eng-ML): I'll add a unit/regression test into the model onboarding pipeline to run the customer's sample prompts and assert non-refusal for allowed patterns.

Marta (SRE): monitoring: setting alert on sudden refusal rate delta > 10% for customers with triage routes. Will keep INC-4521 open until v2 safety mapping updated and deployed.

Aisha (CS): thanks team. I'll send MediAssist a timeline: immediate pin done, we'll follow up within 48h with a plan and target date for a config fix. Please @mention if you need anything from CS (more transcripts, access). :thumbsup:
